script: "People died in ICE custody, yet I voted—now my conscience is ruined.". I am not going to start with "you're wrong" because that's the exact thing the story says you're doing. I'll just drop into the first line: "You didn't believe us when we shouted 'Black Lives Matter'." I am sitting here, coffee cold, scrolling through the feed, and I see the same people who still think a woman can't be president. They either stayed home or, God forbid, voted for Trump. Sigh. Fast forward to last year: a record‑breaking number of people died in ICE custody. I am like, "Did you even notice?" They're picking up U.S. citizens, deporting them, ignoring court orders. A veteran who'd lived in this country 50 years got a removal order and had to leave. He wasn't a ghost; he was a man who grew up on a base and now had to walk out of his own homeland. ICE is pulling kids from their moms, taking asylum seekers, and still you're like, "Whatever." And then there's Keith Porter Jr., murdered by an off‑duty agent. Geraldo Luis Campos, dead from asphyxiation in ICE custody. Renee Good, the woman who was shot, and you think she deserved it. Alex Petti, just having a gun, and you're like, "He deserved to die." I am not here to lecture; I am here to spill the tea. The audacity of people who turn a blind eye to this—because they're too busy voting for the guy who signed it all into law—has to be addressed. I am better than that. I am not going to stay silent when the system is tearing families apart and killing veterans. I am not going to let the same old narrative drown in the noise. So yeah, leave the sub if you can't see the damage, but for those who can, keep watching. This isn't stopping unless something drastic happens, and it's not going to stop because people are asleep at the wheel. The loop's closed, the tension's real, and the truth is out there.
